title: Maximal ideal and structural map in an affine strict-henselization chart
statement: Let S be a scheme, Ω an algebraically closed field, R a commutative ring, i : Spec R → S an open immersion and xR : Spec Ω → Spec R. Put s = xR followed by i and C = [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the coordinate ring of S_(s). There exist a local-ring structure on C and a ring map ρ : R → C such that Spec(ρ) followed by i is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] and the maximal ideal of C is the extension under ρ of the prime xR(closedPoint Ω).

source.place: Tag 04HX, affine-chart colimit identification; Tag 04GW, triple colimit; Tag 04GP, property (4). Sources read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX, /04GW and /04GP.

proof.text: Apply etale_local_ring_triples to i and xR. Retain the chart equivalence E, the diagram isomorphism delta, its R-map compatibility, colimit cocones cn and ct, and the colimit isomorphism t with its coprojection formula. Apply strictHenselization_triples over the relative separable closure K to obtain a local triple colimit c, its structure map rho, and maximalIdeal(c) = p.map(rho).

Let G be the inverse small-model equivalence followed by strictHenselizationAffineInclusion. Both functors are equivalences. Supply the full affine diagram D with the returned cocone cn as a HasColimit instance. The explicit final-functor colimit isomorphism Functor.Final.colimitIso G.op D identifies the chosen small ring with colimit D; compose it with colimit.isoColimitCocone ⟨cn,hcn⟩ to obtain e1. Its coprojection formula is Functor.Final.ι_colimitIso_hom followed by the cocone formula, giving colimit.iota(j) followed by e1.hom = cn.iota(G(j)). Compose e1 with the chart-to-triples isomorphism t and the unique comparison ct.pt isomorphic to c.pt to obtain e.

The pointed chart (Spec R, i, xR) is an object chart of the full affine category and belongs to the chart subcategory via the identity of Spec R. Choose a small representative j with an isomorphism phi : G(j) to chart. Define iota0 to be D(phi.op) followed by the small colimit coprojection at j. The coprojection formula for e1 and naturality of cn give iota0 followed by e1.hom = cn.iota(chart). Use the compatibility of delta with the identity chart, the formula for t and uniqueness of ct-to-c to obtain GammaSpecIso(R).inv followed by iota0 followed by e.hom = rho. Cancel e.hom. If u : Spec B to Spec R is the scheme map underlying phi, then u followed by i is the structure map of G(j). Naturality of toSpecGamma identifies the spectrum of the chart ring map with the limit leg at j followed by u. The defining equation strictHenselizationStructuralMap_eq at j therefore gives the required structural-map equality.

Transport the local-ring instance from c.pt along e.inv. Map maximalIdeal(c) = p.map(rho) through e.inv and use Mathlib IsLocalRing.map_ringEquiv_maximalIdeal and Ideal.map_map. The point p defined by SpecToEquivOfField is definitionally xR(closedPoint Omega). This gives the required equality for rho followed by e.inv.

lean.statement: theorem strictHenselization_chart_maximalIdeal {S : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (i : Spec R ⟶ S) [IsOpenImmersion i] (xR : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R) : ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (strictHenselizationRing (xR ≫ i))) (ρ : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing (xR ≫ i)), Spec.map ρ ≫ i = strictHenselizationStructuralMap (xR ≫ i) ∧ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (strictHenselizationRing (xR ≫ i)) = (xR (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)).asIdeal.map ρ.hom
